Subject: Pricing + model list for hosted API

Hi Jonas,

We're evaluating providers for a hosted inference integration and I was hoping you could share your standard per-1M token pricing (separately for input and output), plus a current roster of supported models (default, quantized variants, any Redwood-optimized variants).

Quick context: Silverline is aiming for a public beta in Q4. Expected baseline is ~10M tokens/month for the initial product, with a potential scale to ~500M/mo if the beta goes well. Helpful to understand:
- Per-1M token input vs output rates
- Which models are recommended for chat vs single-turn generation
- Any special notes on how streaming or function/tool output is billed
- Volume breakpoints and standard discounts for a 12-month commit

Could you send a simple IO rate table and the model catalog (or a link)? If you have a one-sheet ratecard that covers hosted API tiers, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Claire Dunn

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Hi Claire — great to hear from you, and congrats on the Q4 goal. See the quick answers below and I attached our hosted ratecard for a compact reference (redwood_hosted_ratecard_q2_2028.pdf).

Short answers first:
- Input vs output: we charge separately for tokens sent in (prompt/context) and tokens generated (completion/response).
- Streaming/output: streaming responses are billed on output tokens as they are emitted; function calls are billed as normal completion tokens.
- Model roster: included in the attached ratecard and summarized inline.

Per-1M token baseline (hosted API, list prices, USD):
- Small (~7B, low-latency): input $25 / 1M, output $45 / 1M
- Medium (13B–34B): input $50 / 1M, output $90 / 1M
- Large (70B+): input $200 / 1M, output $380 / 1M
- Redwood-Optimized (quantized variants available): input $120 / 1M, output $210 / 1M

Notes:
- These are list (pay-as-you-go) hosted rates. Input+output are additive for billing.
- Embeddings are separate (usually $15 / 1M embedding tokens for our standard embedder) — included in the PDF model roster.
- We support float and quantized execution paths; quantized variants are typically ~20–40% cheaper at inference cost depending on model and quality settings.

Attachments: redwood_hosted_ratecard_q2_2028.pdf (PDF, 125KB) — contains model roster, IO examples, and common discount tiers.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call if you want to walk through breakpoints and commit options.

Best,

Claire — thanks for the follow-ups. Pasted below is the straightforward schedule you can share with finance; I've also flagged this deal in HubSpot (link below) and attached the same ratecard for procurement.

Billing basics
- Input and output are billed separately and add together for the invoice. Example: 1M input + 1M output on a Medium model = $50 + $90 = $140.

Quantized variants
- We publish alternate per-1M lines for our Redwood-Optimized quantized variants in the attached ratecard. Typical effective savings vs list: 20–35% depending on model and sequence-length/profile. For planning, assume a 25% reduction for quantized medium models.

Standard commit discount schedule (hosted API, illustrative):
- No commit (pay-as-you-go): list rates (see earlier)
- 3-month prepaid (>=25M total over term): 10% off list
- 6-month prepaid (>=100M total over term): 18% off list
- 12-month prepaid (>=600M total over term): 25% off list
- Large enterprise/strategic (500M+/mo + dedicated capacity): custom pricing (typically 30–40%+ and Reserved Capacity through Redwood Dedicated)

Operational guidance at ~500M tokens/mo
- Hosted: we can handle 500M/mo on hosted with predictable performance; recommend: enable KV caching for common prefixes, set autoscaling burst limits, and use moderate batching (we can recommend default batch sizes for your latency SLO).
- Dedicated: if you need strict latency SLAs, consistent tail latency, and higher discounts, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) is the better path — it also unlocks compute-reserved pricing and higher burst capacity without throttling.

Next steps
